checks.detail: the good PDF must succeed even though four siblings failed
a failing document must not abort the drain
claim (f) is about diagnosability: an error column reading 'Exception: ' is a silent failure wearing a label
what a downstream UI can actually pattern-match on
markdown is empty for all four, so retry_failed must route to pending_source
the drain never silently re-attempts failures; a re-drain after an explicit retry re-attempts and the systematic problem surfaces again
the good PDF plus the newly-fixed path
retry_failed routes purely by markdown emptiness, not by a remembered stage — markdown is present, so the conversion must not be redone

the markdown-bearing document must NOT be re-converted — the in-process cross-check of the same checkpoint guarantee claim (c) tests against a process kill. Conversions of the still-broken sources are counted separately and are expected
still-broken sources re-converted by the same retry — expected and correct: they carry no markdown, so pending_source is the right stage
